title: NRI Tax on Gifts to HUF: What You Need to Know
description: Gifting money from your NRO bank account to a Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) does not create any tax liability for you, the Non-Resident Indian (NRI) giver. Ind.

faq.q: Is the NRI taxed on giving the gift to an HUF?
faq.a: No, the Non-Resident Indian (NRI) making the gift of money is not subject to any income tax liability in India on the act of giving the gift. The tax implications, if any, arise for the recipient HUF.

faq.q: Is a gift deed mandatory when gifting money to an HUF?
faq.a: While not strictly mandatory for cash gifts, it is highly recommended to execute a gift deed. It provides legal proof of the transaction, establishes the genuineness of the gift, and can prevent future disputes or scrutiny from tax authorities.

faq.q: Can an NRI gift immovable property to an HUF?
faq.a: Yes, an NRI can gift immovable property to an HUF. However, the tax implications for the HUF would then be based on the stamp duty value of the property, and specific regulations regarding transfer of immovable property to/from NRIs would apply.

faq.q: What is the tax threshold for gifts received by an HUF?
faq.a: If an HUF receives gifts of money from non-relatives, and the aggregate value of such gifts exceeds ₹50,000 in a financial year, the entire amount received (not just the excess) becomes taxable as "Income from Other Sources" for the HUF.

faq.q: Who is considered a 'relative' for HUF gift tax purposes?
faq.a: For an HUF, any 'member' of that specific HUF is considered a 'relative'. Gifts received by the HUF from its members are exempt from tax, irrespective of the amount.

faq.q: Can an NRI gift from their NRE account to an HUF?
faq.a: Yes, an NRI can gift from their NRE account to an HUF. Funds from NRE accounts are freely repatriable and tax-exempt in the hands of the NRI, but the taxability for the HUF recipient remains the same as per Section 56(2)(x).

faq.q: What records should an HUF maintain for gifts received?
faq.a: An HUF should maintain a copy of the gift deed, bank statements showing the receipt of funds, and any other relevant correspondence. These documents are crucial for substantiating the nature and source of the funds during tax assessments.
